thesis: Micron reported record fiscal Q4 results (EPS $33.42, revenue $54.23B) with above-consensus Q1 guidance, and management says memory shortages could persist for years; Goldman and Mizuho raised targets. The stock slipped ~2% today and sits ~14% below its 52-week high, but that is price action after a +32% 60-day run rather than any change in the disclosed results or guidance, so it does not change the read. No scheduled binary event before the next review.
invalidation: Guidance cut or evidence memory pricing/supply tightness is reversing

thesis: SpaceX has had a run of confirmed operating milestones (Starship reaching orbit and deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites, NASA Crew-13 launch) and the stock gained ~7% today on Musk's comments about powering Nvidia AI hardware, which is partly sentiment. Analysts average a Moderate Buy. Evidence is a mix of confirmed events and commentary, with no counter-case engaged; limited trading history (recent listing).
invalidation: Launch failure or loss of key contract/customer; reversal of AI-infrastructure narrative

thesis: Intel is up ~32% over 60 days on a sector-wide chip/AI rally and Meta-related CPU-demand expectations; the move is largely sentiment and read-through from Micron's results rather than a new Intel disclosure, though Q2 revenue (+25% YoY, DCAI +59%) supports the narrative. Earnings on Oct 22 are an unresolved binary and the price is well extended; the evidence is mixed rather than a clear net read.
invalidation: Weak Oct 22 earnings or guidance; fade of the AI CPU-demand narrative

thesis: AMD hit all-time highs and a $1T market cap on confirmed deals (OpenAI 6GW Instinct deployment, $5B Anthropic commitment) and a planned Q4 price increase. Valuation (P/E ~158, +183% YTD) is the main counter-point and is not resolved by the evidence; the stock is within ~2% of its 52-week high. Multiple contributing factors, none clearly dominant.
invalidation: Deployment delays or deal scale-back; sharp multiple compression in AI semis

thesis: Dell raised FY27 revenue guidance to $192B (from $167B) with record AI-server orders ($60.9B) and a $95B backlog, and joined a $15B+ Japan AI data center plan. UBS argues the near-doubling in the stock leaves limited further upside; that valuation counter-case is not dismissed here. Catalyst is real and company-specific but the setup is stretched (+26% in 60 days).
invalidation: Guidance walked back or AI-server orders/backlog decelerate

thesis: Qorvo is trading on its pending $22B merger with Skyworks ($32.50 cash + 0.96 SWKS per share); the 4x volume spike and +25% 60-day move reflect the deal timeline being pulled forward to year-end. Remaining China and South Korea antitrust approvals are an unresolved binary, and merger-arb pricing limits the independent upside, so this is not a favorable standalone entry.
invalidation: N/A (avoid) — would revisit if deal terminated or after closing

thesis: Marvell posted record revenue (+36.5% YoY) and raised guidance, and the stock is up ~38% over 60 days, still ~17% below its 52-week high. Insider selling (CEO, COO trust under preset plans) and the Oct 6 Investor Day are pending/unresolved factors; the read is constructive but no single factor is clearly dominant.
invalidation: Investor Day or next guidance disappoints; AI-networking demand slows

thesis: Nvidia's board added $150B to its buyback (total $235B authorization) and customers (Anthropic, xAI, OpenAI) have large multi-year compute commitments; the stock made a new 52-week high today. Extended valuation after a +12% 60-day move and the China chip-sales question are open points not resolved by this evidence.
invalidation: Hyperscaler capex cuts or loss of major compute commitments

thesis: AXT posted record Q2 revenue ($47.6M, +164% YoY) and 45% gross margin on indium-phosphide demand for AI optical connectivity, and was added to the S&P SmallCap 600. Offsetting: extreme valuation (P/E >4000) and $78.8M of insider sales over 12 months. Q3 earnings Oct 29 are a pending catalyst.
invalidation: Q3 results/guide miss or loss of indium-phosphide demand momentum

thesis: SK hynix is benefiting from tight AI-memory supply (contract repricing, strong HBM demand) and Micron's strong results read across to the group; shares are ~20% higher over the past month and within ~2.4% of the 52-week high. Earnings on Oct 27 are pending and part of the move is sector-wide, so no single company-specific factor is clearly dominant.
invalidation: Memory pricing rolls over or HBM share loss; weak Oct 27 results
